in_text_mentions: included intrauterine growth retardation (IUGR), brachymelia, and brachydactyly. Craniofacial dysmorphia comprised a prominent occiput and a flat face with bitemporal narrowing, hypertelorism, short flat upturned nose, long smooth philtrum, microretrognathia, and low set, dorsally rotated ears (Figure 1a–f). The severity score in Cases 3 to 5 ranged from >30 to 45, thus corresponding to a “more severe classical manifestation” of the disorder, whereas Case 7, presenting with bilateral renal agenesis and a severity score of 60, had to be classified as a “severe and lethal manifestation” of SLOS.

and Dandy‐Walker cyst (Figures 2, 3, 4). Typical facial dysmorphisms, already recognizable in midterm fetuses, and toe II/III syndactyly completed the pattern of characteristic SLOS features (Figure 1). panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Frontal clinical photograph of an infant patient (7 months old per in-text) from a DHCR7 mild-phenotype Smith-Lemli-Opitz case; shows mild facial dysmorphism with epicanthal folds (epicanthus stated in text) consistent with SLOS. Eyes are anonymized with a black censor bar. Findings limited to the epicanthal folds supported by caption/in-text; anteverted auricles noted as a proposed finding. Attenuated/mild expression consistent with the reported mild phenotype (variant typicality). [raw subtype: mild phenotype] B: Clinical photograph of the infant patient's feet held in an adult hand, visibly showing bilateral cutaneous syndactyly of the second and third toes. 2-3 toe syndactyly is the classic, highly characteristic skeletal manifestation of Smith-Lemli-Opitz Syndrome, and the caption and in-text explicitly attribute it to patient 2 with a confirmed DHCR7 mild-phenotype SLOS diagnosis. Classic presentation. [raw subtype: mild phenotype]

panels.rationale: Clinical photograph of the genital area from a documented Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome case report. The caption and in-text description explicitly state small penis with hypospadias and undescended testis, which represent undervirilized external genitalia, a recognized manifestation of SLOS. The image is a real human patient photograph with no third-party copyright indicated.

in_text_mentions: Physical examination: the infant had microcephaly, broad nasal tip, maxillary hypoplasia gingival enlargement, low set ears, (Fig. 1) ptosis and staphyloschisis (Fig. 2), the limbs hadsyndactyly of second and third toes (Fig. 3). Cardiovascular system examination showed short systolic murmure at lower left sternal borderin. Genital examination showed small penis hypospadiasis with undescended testis (Fig. 4). The baby had dry mucous membranes and tachycardia.

panels.rationale: Supine abdominal/pelvic radiograph from a confirmed adult Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome case report showing multiple radio-opaque paperclips lying within the pelvic cavity, captioned as 'Abdominal X-ray with paperclips embedded in the pelvic floor.' Self-injurious object insertion is a recognized behavioral manifestation of the SLOS phenotype, and the article documents this patient's repeated insertion of paperclips and needles. The radiograph is a real patient image of a specific, though behavioral/complicational, manifestation rather than a classic SLOS dysmorphic feature, so no vocabulary finding key applies (a placeholder AV canal defect entry is marked evidence-free and findings are placed in proposed_findings); confidence is therefore moderate.

panels.figure_caption: Abdominal X-ray with paperclips embedded in the pelvic floor.
in_text_mentions: empt to stimulate his heart by inserting paperclips and sewing needles through his thoracic wall into his myocardium (Figure 1). He described no pain whatsoever, but enjoyed the resulting palpitations. The patient returned again to the operating room four years later, where multiple sewing needles and a paperclip were removed from his pericardium and myocardium (Figure 2). Over the following years, the patient began inserting paperclips into his abdominal cavity. The paperclips slowly migrated through his peritoneal cavity and became embedded within his pelvic floor musculature (Figures 3, 4).
